title: feat(verify): add on-demand proof scenarios and a verify skill
body:
A UI criterion in a PR needs a screenshot or a video from the real app as its proof row, and there was no repeatable way to produce one. Each author had to improvise a launch, a capture and an upload.

## What this does

- Adds `.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md`: a project skill that maps scenarios (command, what it shows, artifacts) and says how to run one and attach the output to a PR's `## Proof` table.
- Adds `apps/kaipu-record/verify/` with three scenarios (`launch`, `library`, `export`) that drive the built Electron app with Playwright `_electron.launch`, take `page.screenshot` at named steps and record `recordVideo`. Output goes to the gitignored `apps/kaipu-record/test-results/verify/<scenario>/`.
- Adds `proof` and `proof:run` package scripts, and an optional `recordVideoDir` parameter on the e2e `launchApp` helper.

## Why

Design: the "Verification on the real surface" and "The proof list" sections of the [development pipeline](https://github.com/csdev19/general-knowledge/blob/main/conventions/development-pipeline.md). The driver's own recording runs unattended and needs no screen-recording permission. The scenarios reuse `launchApp`, so userData and the vault are throwaway and seeded, same as the e2e suite.

This does not touch CI. ADR 0006 and ADR 0027 stay as written: the macOS e2e suite still runs only on release candidates. `verify/` is outside `e2e/`, matches `*.verify.ts` (not `*.e2e.ts`), and has its own config, so `test:e2e` never picks it up.

## What to review

1. **`apps/kaipu-record/e2e/helpers/launch.ts:84,116`** — the only change to existing code: an optional `recordVideoDir` forwarded to `electron.launch`. Check that with no argument the launch is identical to before.
2. **`apps/kaipu-record/verify/helpers.ts:20-55`** — `startScenario` wipes the scenario folder, `finish()` closes the app (which finalizes the video), keeps the largest `.webm` as `video.webm` and deletes the others. Decide whether dropping the small per-window clips is right (the app opens overlay windows; they are tiny).
3. **`.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md:20-35`** — the run instructions, including the inline `MAIN_VITE_*` build step. Check that the wording matches how you build locally.
4. **`apps/kaipu-record/package.json:18-19`** — script names. `proof` avoids the root `bun run verify`, which ADR 0006 says deliberately contains no e2e.

**Safe to skim:** `verify/*.verify.ts` (locators copied from `e2e/export.e2e.ts`, `library.e2e.ts`, `helpers/launch.ts`), `verify/playwright.config.ts`.

## Proof

| Criterion | What was done | How to check it | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| A scenario launches the real app and writes screenshots and a video | Ran `bun run proof:run` (all three scenarios) on macOS | `cd apps/kaipu-record && bun run proof:run`, then `ls -la test-results/verify/*` | `3 passed (16.3s)`; files below |
| Artifacts are not committed | `test-results` is in the root `.gitignore` | `git check-ignore -v apps/kaipu-record/test-results/verify/launch/video.webm` | `.gitignore:65:test-results` |
| The captured screenshot shows the criterion | Opened `export/03-ready-to-share.png` | Open the file | "Ready to share · 0.1 MB" card over the editor, with "View file" |

Run output (second run, after the helper change; the first run had the same 3 passes):

```
[verify] export: 01-editor.png (120618 bytes)
[verify] export: 02-export-sheet.png (145936 bytes)
[verify] export: 03-ready-to-share.png (126544 bytes)
[verify] export: video.webm (259584 bytes)
[verify] launch: 01-onboarding.png (72954 bytes)
[verify] launch: 02-main-window.png (59468 bytes)
[verify] launch: video.webm (91904 bytes)
[verify] library: 01-library-list.png (60268 bytes)
[verify] library: 02-recording-detail.png (77710 bytes)
[verify] library: video.webm (151522 bytes)
  3 passed (16.3s)
```

A final `bun run proof:run launch` after formatting: exit 0, 1 passed, `video.webm` 81972 bytes.

## Decisions

- **Reuse `launchApp` with one optional parameter** instead of a second launch helper, so the seeded vault and the locale pin cannot drift from the e2e suite.
- **Separate `verify/` folder and config**, not an `e2e/` project, so a proof run can never be counted as, or change, the e2e tier.
- **Script names `proof` / `proof:run`**, not `verify`, to avoid colliding with the root `verify` script.
- **One `video.webm` per scenario** (largest clip).
- The files are not uploaded to this PR: they are local and gitignored, so the table cites the run output. The skill explains uploading through the GitHub UI.

## Verify it yourself

```
cd apps/kaipu-record
MAIN_VITE_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:3000 MAIN_VITE_WEB_URL=http://localhost:3001 bunx electron-vite build
bun run proof:run launch
ls -la test-results/verify/launch
```

## What I did not verify

- Linux and Windows. `export` self-skips on Linux (no H.264 encoder); `launch` and `library` were not run there.
- That the scenarios behave the same on a machine with a real `.env`. The build used placeholder `MAIN_VITE_*` URLs, so cloud or auth paths were not exercised.
- The `bun run proof` (build + run) script was not run end to end; I ran the build and `proof:run` separately.
- Video content was not watched, only written with non-trivial size. One screenshot was opened and checked.

## Checks

- `bunx oxlint apps/kaipu-record/verify apps/kaipu-record/e2e`: exit 0, 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `bunx oxfmt --check` on touched files: exit 0
- `bun run check-types` (apps/kaipu-record): exit 0; `verify/` also type-checked with a temporary tsconfig extending `tsconfig.node.json` (no errors; the temp file was removed)
- `bun run proof:run`: exit 0, 3 passed
